code.originalText: Seven-month review after an exacerbation: lungs, opioid therapy, mood, safety, weight, and vaccines

text.paragraph: Seven-month review after an exacerbation: lungs, opioid therapy, mood, safety, weight, and vaccines. [S]

Ms. Barrett Browning returns seven months after diagnosis and ten weeks after an exacerbation of bronchiectasis, treated at home with amoxicillin for 14 days; the culture from that visit grew Haemophilus influenzae sensitive to amoxicillin, and she was back to her usual sputum within two weeks. She has had no blood since. She finished her sixteen grief sessions in July and had one booster session last month. She has stayed at morphine solution 4 mL twice daily since June, by her choice through the summer and the chest infection, and now asks for the next small step. She is writing every day and has gained weight. [S]

text.paragraph: Vital signs recorded on 1845-10-19; see the Vital Signs section. [S]

tr.td: A few crackles at the left base; no wheeze
Warm and engaged; no suicidal ideation

Chronic cough with daily yellow sputum, occasional streaks of blood, and breathlessness on stairs, worse in winter, for several years after an illness with blood in the sputum about eight years ago; tuberculosis, nontuberculous mycobacteria and bronchiectasis to be distinguished
S — Synthetic presenting concern at the index visit, superseded by the diagnosis at the consultation; it echoes her documented chest illness (D).

Non-cystic fibrosis bronchiectasis of the left lower lobe and lingula with chronic Haemophilus influenzae infection and mild airflow obstruction (Bronchiectasis Severity Index 3, mild); tuberculosis and nontuberculous mycobacterial disease excluded; synthetic modern diagnosis chosen for a historical chest illness whose cause is disputed
S — Synthetic modern diagnosis; the nature of her historical chest illness remains undetermined (R, disputed).

Long-term prescribed opioid therapy (oral morphine 20 mg a day for many years, for cough, sleeplessness and palpitations), with expected physiological dependence; no opioid use disorder on DSM-5-TR assessment
S — Synthetic modern problem anchored to her documented prescribed opium (D); tolerance and withdrawal on prescribed opioids do not count toward opioid use disorder.

Prolonged grief disorder after the drowning of her closest brother five years ago, with yearning, self-blame, avoidance of reminders of the sea, and depressive symptoms (PHQ-9 12); no suicidal ideation
S — Synthetic modern diagnosis anchored to her documented bereavement (D); not a claim about her real mental health.
Vitamin D deficiency (25-hydroxyvitamin D 15 ng/mL) in a woman who rarely goes outdoors
S — Synthetic finding at intake; repleted by twelve weeks.

Exacerbation of bronchiectasis (more sputum, purulent sputum, more cough and breathlessness for three days, with low-grade fever), treated with amoxicillin for 14 days and more frequent airway clearance; resolved
S — Synthetic intercurrent exacerbation; not a historical claim.

Bronchiectasis (J47.9). Back to baseline after one exacerbation in seven months; CRP 3.2 mg/L and white count 7.4. The sputum culture sent last week grew normal flora only. With fewer than three exacerbations a year, long-term macrolide is not needed. [S]
Continue airway clearance twice daily.
Influenza vaccine today; COVID-19 vaccine at her pharmacy this month.
Spirometry, Bronchiectasis Severity Index and mycobacterial culture at one year.

Keep the exacerbation plan and rescue antibiotic at home.

Long-term opioid therapy: third step (Z79.891). Down from 20 to 16 mg a day over seven months with no troublesome withdrawal and better sleep and cough; still no opioid use disorder. She chooses a third small step. She may decide to stay at any dose that suits her. [S]
Morphine solution 3.5 mL (7 mg) twice daily from today.
Prescription monitoring program checked.

Prolonged grief disorder, improving (F43.81). PHQ-9 5 from 12 at intake: a response, close to remission. No suicidal ideation. [S]

Underweight, improving (R63.6). 44.2 kg from 41.5 kg; BMI 17.9. [S]

list.item: Tuberculosis excluded and a diagnosis for the cough within two weeks. Outcome by 1845-03-23: Smears, NAAT and IGRA negative within a week; bronchiectasis diagnosed by CT at one week [S]

Airway clearance twice daily, with less sputum and no blood in it, by three months. Outcome by 1845-06-15: Airway clearance twice daily; sputum down from about four to one tablespoon a day; no blood since the first month [S]

Safe opioid therapy: naloxone at home, no overdose or sedation, and any dose change only by her choice. Outcome by 1845-10-19: Naloxone at home; no sedation; she chose to reduce from 20 to 14 mg a day over seven months without troublesome withdrawal [S]
Response of grief and depressive symptoms (PHQ-9 down by at least half) by six months. Outcome by 1845-10-19: PHQ-9 5 from 12 after sixteen sessions of grief therapy; she can speak of her brother [S]
Weight up toward a BMI of 18.5 (45.6 kg) by seven months. Outcome by 1845-10-19: 44.2 kg from 41.5 kg (BMI 17.9); still gaining [S]
Vitamin D above 30 ng/mL by twelve weeks. Outcome by 1845-06-15: 34 ng/mL [S]
